proofs.proof_tex:
Under \(\texttt{ass:one-unsupported-row}\) and
\(\texttt{ass:binary-free-row}\), the generalized unsupported-row objects
specialize to
\[
 \mathcal R_{\mathrm{free}}=\{rstar\},
 \qquad
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{free}}
 =\{(1-q,q):0\leq q\leq 1\}.
\]
Comparing \(\texttt{def:model-class}\) with
\(\texttt{def:finite-unsupported-model-class}\), all the remaining
membership requirements are identical: the same finite schema and graph
are used, the same source and target groundings are induced, the ground
noises are mutually independent, mechanisms are type shared, the source
laws \(Psrc\) are reproduced, and the rows in \(K\) are used at all
positive-source-support keys.  Hence, in this specialization,
\(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{fin}}=Mone\).  The two query definitions then give
\(Q_{\mathrm{fin}}=Q\).  Finally, replaying
\(\texttt{def:multivariate-target-polynomial}\) with
\(p_{rstar}=(1-q,q)\) is exactly the replay defining \(F\); equivalently,
this is the equality proved in \(\texttt{lem:polynomial-reduction}\).
Thus
\[
 \Phi\bigl((1-q,q)\bigr)=F(q),\qquad 0\leq q\leq1.
\]
Applying \(\texttt{thm:sharp-finite-unsupported-rows}\) to this
specialization yields
\[
 \Theta=F([0,1]).
\]
In particular, the reverse inclusion is witnessed by compatible
finite-noise, type-shared models and is not merely an outer bound.

It remains to identify the endpoints appearing in the statement.  The
polynomial \(F\) is continuous.  Therefore it attains a minimum and a
maximum on the compact interval \([0,1]\), as also follows from the compact
attainment argument in
\(\texttt{thm:sharp-finite-unsupported-rows}\).  If \(F\) is nonconstant
and \(c\in(0,1)\) is either optimizer, then for every sufficiently small
\(h>0\) the two one-sided difference quotients at \(c\) have the
appropriate opposite weak signs.  Differentiability gives
\[
 F'(c)
 =\lim_{h\downarrow0}\frac{F(c+h)-F(c)}{h}
 =\lim_{h\downarrow0}\frac{F(c)-F(c-h)}{h}=0.
\]
Consequently every optimizer is either \(0\), \(1\), or a feasible
distinct real root of \(F'\), and hence belongs to \(Ccrit\) by
\(\texttt{def:critical-candidates}\).  Conversely \(Ccrit\subseteq[0,1]\).
It follows from the definitions of \(L\) and \(U\) that
\[
 \min_{q\in[0,1]}F(q)=\min_{c\in Ccrit}F(c)=L,
 \qquad
 \max_{q\in[0,1]}F(q)=\max_{c\in Ccrit}F(c)=U.
\]
If \(F\) is constant, all candidate and interval values coincide, so the
same two equalities hold.  The continuous image of an interval is
connected, while compactness makes it closed and bounded; therefore its
image is precisely the interval between its attained extrema:
\[
 \Theta=F([0,1])=[L,U].
\]

We next justify the comparator qualifications.  By
\(\texttt{lem:ejaz-bareinboim-rho-markovian-scope}\), the
Ejaz--Bareinboim \(\rho\)-Markovian class permits a ground instance to
have shared exogenous parents.  A model in \(Mone\) is the special case
with no such sharing, because
\(\texttt{ass:markovian-noises}\) makes the noises of distinct ground
endogenous variables mutually independent.  Its observed domains are
finite by \(\texttt{ass:finite-domains}\), and the fixed finite ground
graphs have a finite uniform bound on relational-parent multiset size.
Thus \(Mone\) is a subclass of that comparator class, and the inclusion
can be strict when additional within-instance latent confounding is
allowed.

If \(F\) is nonconstant, choose \(q_1,q_2\in[0,1]\) with
\(F(q_1)\neq F(q_2)\).  The already proved reverse inclusion supplies
\(M_1,M_2\in Mone\) such that
\[
 Q(M_1)=F(q_1)\neq F(q_2)=Q(M_2).
\]
Both models also belong to the larger comparator class.  Hence the query
is not point identified there either.  A report of
\(\mathsf{FAIL}\) by the comparator procedure does not alter the equality
\(\Theta=[L,U]\) for \(Mone\), but none of the preceding inclusions bounds
the values of the extra confounded models; sharpness for the larger class
is therefore not asserted.  If \(F\) is constant, the first part gives
\(L=U\) and point identification on \(Mone\).  This conclusion transfers
to the comparator class when the supplied graph excludes its additional
shared-exogenous structures, because the two compatible classes then
coincide.  Without class equality, constancy on a subclass supplies no
conclusion about the extra elements of a strict superclass.

For completeness, unsupportedness by itself does not force failure.  A
two-node acyclic target with a supported fair binary node \(A\), an
unsupported binary node \(X\) having success probability \(q\), independent
ground noises, and event \(B=\{A=X\}\) has
\[
 P(B\mid\operatorname{do}(a))
 =(1-q)\frac12+q\frac12=\frac12,
\]
although the row of \(X\) occurs directly in every event term.  Thus the
unsupported row can cancel from the query.  Type sharing is load bearing
for the asserted one-parameter class: with two independent target nodes
using the same unsupported binary key and the event of exactly one
success, the shared-row map is
\[
 2q(1-q)\leq\frac12.
\]
If type sharing is removed while all other features of this finite
acyclic example are retained, occurrence-specific probabilities
\(q_1=1\) and \(q_2=0\) make the event probability one.  This supplies the
required small-instance check and shows why the common coordinate \(q\)
cannot be replaced silently by occurrence-specific rows.

By \(\texttt{thm:sharp-one-row}\) and the definitions of the selected
candidates, \(qminus,qplus\in[0,1]\) and
\[
 F(qminus)=L,\qquad F(qplus)=U.
\]
We analyze the breakpoint construction directly, once with
\(q_\circ=qminus\) and once with \(q_\circ=qplus\).

Fix an endogenous type \(t\) with ordered outcome alphabet
\(\mathcal X_t=\{1,\ldots,k_t\}\).  For every explicit context \(c\) of
that type, let
\[
 0=s_{c,0}\leq s_{c,1}\leq\cdots\leq s_{c,k_t}=1
\]
be the cumulative probabilities of its prescribed row.  At a supported
context these numbers are rational because \(K\) is rational.  At the
free binary context they are \(0,q_\circ,1\).  Let
\(0=u_0<u_1<\cdots<u_J=1\) be the sorted set of all distinct cumulative
thresholds for type \(t\).  Give its type-level noise the atom
\(e_j\) with mass
\[
 \mu_t(e_j)=u_j-u_{j-1},\qquad 1\leq j\leq J.
\]
These masses are nonnegative and telescope to one.  For context \(c\),
define the common mechanism on atom \(e_j\) to be the unique category
\(\ell\) for which an interior point of
\((u_{j-1},u_j)\) lies in \((s_{c,\ell-1},s_{c,\ell})\).
Because every \(s_{c,\ell}\) is one of the \(u_j\), no interval crosses a
context threshold, so this category is well defined.  Summing atom masses
over the intervals assigned to categories \(1,\ldots,\ell\) telescopes
to \(s_{c,\ell}\).  Therefore the mechanism realizes exactly the
prescribed conditional row at every context.

Use the same table for every occurrence of type \(t\), and give distinct
ground nodes independent copies of its noise law.  This proves type
sharing and the independent-ground-noise condition.  In an acyclic source
grounding, topological induction now gives the product of the prescribed
conditional rows: at a root the claim is immediate, and conditional on
the already generated parents the next node has exactly its prescribed
row and an independent noise draw.  The product equals the supplied source
law by \(\texttt{ass:source-compatibility}\), so every table in \(Psrc\)
is reproduced exactly.  The same induction after deleting the
intervened factors gives the target truncated factorization.  Its value is
\(F(q_\circ)\) by the defining replay of \(F\).  Hence the two
constructed models belong to \(Mone\) and satisfy
\[
 Q(Mminus)=F(qminus)=L,\qquad
 Q(Mplus)=F(qplus)=U.
\]

The record \(Z\) lists each ordered breakpoint, adjacent-interval mass,
and context-specific output on every atom.  At every source and target
node in \(Ictx\), it stores the node label, parent tuple, context key,
intervention status, and a reference to the appropriate common type
table.  Since \(Ictx\) exhaustively fixes those occurrences, these records
determine every induced source and target grounding without introducing
an occurrence-specific mechanism.

Each explicit context contributes at most \(k_t-1\) internal cumulative
thresholds.  Thus the union of \(0\), \(1\), and all internal thresholds
has at most
\[
 2+\sum_c(k_t-1)
\]
distinct points, and hence at most
\[
 1+\sum_c(|\mathcal X_t|-1)
\]
positive adjacent-interval atoms.  Duplicate thresholds and zero-length
intervals can only reduce this count.

All supported thresholds are rational.  If \(q_\circ\) is rational, every
adjacent difference is rational.  If it is irrational, it lies strictly
between two consecutive thresholds \(a<b\) from the rational threshold
set before insertion.  Inserting it replaces the rational mass \(b-a\)
by
\[
 q_\circ-a\quad\hbox{and}\quad b-q_\circ.
\]
These are the only two possibly irrational masses, and both are affine in
the selected algebraic optimizer.  If the selected optimizer is \(0\),
\(1\), or an already present rational threshold, duplicate removal adds no
positive atom.  This proves all assertions, including boundary
coincidences.

Assume
\[
 Check(S,G,Rsrc,Psrc,\rho,a,B,Ictx,K,F,Z,\Gamma)=1.
\]
By the definition of \(Check\), every guarded check in
\(\texttt{def:checker}\) has returned true.  We show successively what
those checks imply.

First, the checker recomputes the injective, length-delimited canonical
digest from the supplied fixed instance and \(Z\).  Equality with the
digest stored in \(\Gamma\) therefore gives equality of the entire encoded
tuples, rather than merely equality of an ambiguous concatenation.  The
schema-reference, edge-reference, lexicographic-index, and acyclicity
checks then show that the accepted \(Ictx\) has one and only one record
for every required source ground node and every event-consistent complete
target-assignment term of the supplied groundings, with the recorded
context, parent tuple, intervention status, and target-relevance flag.
Thus it is their exact incidence table.

For a row claimed to be supported, the checker recomputes its source
parent-context probability and checks that this rational number is
strictly positive before division.  It then divides the corresponding
joint cells by that positive number and compares every result with the
row recorded in \(K\).  Hence all such divisions are defined and \(K\)
contains exactly the recovered target-relevant positive-support rows.
Equality checks between occurrences with the same type--context label
enforce type sharing.  Exhaustiveness of the relevance records, followed
by the source-support checks, leaves exactly the recorded key \(rstar\)
unsupported.  Finally, each rational addition and multiplication in the
truncated-factorization replay is checked, and the terminal dense
coefficient list is compared coefficient by coefficient with \(F\).
Therefore the supplied polynomial is exactly the causal replay polynomial.

We next analyze the algebraic portion.  The checker verifies an integer
clearing of \(F'\), its gcd data, and its square-free part \(g\).  In the
constant and nonzero-constant-derivative cases it uses the designated
boundary-only record.  Otherwise,
\(\texttt{lem:sturm-root-count-correctness}\) implies that an accepted
rational interval of Sturm count one contains exactly one distinct real
root of \(g\), an interval of count zero contains none, and the checked
variation counts over the disjoint subdivision account for every root.
The feasibility signs retain exactly the roots in \((0,1)\), while the
separate boundary records account for \(0\) and \(1\).  Since a polynomial
and its square-free part have the same distinct roots, repeated roots of
\(F'\) are represented once.  Hence the accepted candidate list is
exactly \(Ccrit\), including all boundary cases.

Fix a listed candidate \(c\).  For an interior candidate, \(g(c)=0\).
In the Sylvester determinant defining that resultant, specialization at
\(z=F(c)\) makes the two input polynomials share the root \(c\), so the
corresponding evaluation matrix has a nonzero kernel and its determinant
vanishes.  The checked resultant identity therefore implies that \(F(c)\)
is a root of the associated value polynomial; for a boundary candidate, exact
rational substitution gives the corresponding assertion.  A resultant
alone could include conjugate or infeasible values, so the checker also
verifies the candidate-specific Sturm--Tarski signs.  If
\(J=(\ell,u)\) is the one-root rational isolator carrying the proposed
value label, those accepted signs give
\[
 \ell<F(c)<u.
\]
The root-count check says that \(J\) contains exactly one root of the
square-free value polynomial.  Thus the linked algebraic number is
necessarily \(F(c)\), not an unrelated conjugate root of the resultant.

The exact sign comparisons totally order distinct value labels.  The
checker assigns a common tie label precisely when the candidate-specific
algebraic equality test succeeds; otherwise disjoint one-root isolators
and strict sign comparisons determine the order.  Therefore equal
interior values, boundary ties, and boundary--interior coincidences are
handled without an invalid numerical separation step.  The selected least
and greatest labels satisfy
\[
 L=\min_{c\in Ccrit}F(c),\qquad
 U=\max_{c\in Ccrit}F(c).
\]
By the critical-point argument in \(\texttt{thm:sharp-one-row}\), these
are also
\[
 L=\min_{q\in[0,1]}F(q),\qquad
 U=\max_{q\in[0,1]}F(q).
\]
An algebraic root having no link from a feasible candidate cannot be
selected.  The same exact sign mechanism checks all
rational-versus-algebraic threshold comparisons, including equality.

Finally, decode \(Z\).  The accepted nonnegativity signs and exact
unit-sum identities make every listed finite-noise table a probability
law.  Shared table labels give one mechanism per endogenous type, and the
node-copy records give mutually independent noise draws at distinct ground
nodes.  The mechanism-output, graph-reference, and incidence checks place
each output in the supplied context and grounding.  Summing the checked
atom masses over output labels recovers every conditional row.  The source
evaluation records multiply these rows in a topological order and agree
cell by cell with \(Psrc\); the positivity checks used above justify every
conditional recovery.  The target records omit exactly the intervened
factors, sum every event-consistent term in \(Ictx\), and agree exactly
with \(L\) and \(U\).  Thus the two decoded models satisfy every clause of
\(\texttt{def:model-class}\), reproduce \(Psrc\), and obey
\[
 Mminus,Mplus\in Mone,\qquad
 Q(Mminus)=L,\qquad Q(Mplus)=U.
\]
All implications used exact identities or certified signs, so repeated
derivative roots, boundary critical points, equal values, algebraic
conjugates, and threshold coincidences do not change the conclusion.

Let
\[
 N=D+LF+T+1.
\]
We construct \(Z\) and \(\Gamma\), show directly that every branch of the
checker accepts, and then bound the construction and verification costs.

Copy the canonical fixed-instance fields, the exhaustive \(Ictx\), and
the supported rational rows into the certificate.  Their length is
\(O(T+LF)\).  The hypothesis that \(F\) is obtained by replaying the
target factorization supplies an ordered list of the additions and
multiplications indexed by the explicit records of \(Ictx\).  Record this
list and its dense intermediate outputs.  There are only polynomially many
gates in the explicit incidence length.  In a product, numerator and
denominator bit lengths add.  In a sum of explicitly many terms, a common
denominator may be chosen as the product of their denominators, so its bit
length is the sum of their bit lengths, and the extra numerator growth is
at most logarithmic in the number of summands plus that denominator
length.  Degrees never exceed the explicitly counted occurrence degree
\(D\).  Hence every recorded rational coefficient has bit length
polynomial in \(N\), and exact gate replay ends at the supplied dense list
\(F\).

Choose \(M>0\) and a primitive \(A\in\mathbb Z[q]\) such that
\[
 F(q)=\frac{A(q)}{M}.
\]
Taking the product of the denominators in the dense input list before
primitive reduction shows that the coefficient bit length \(\tau\) of
\(A\), as well as \(\log M\), is polynomial in \(LF+D+1\).  If \(D=0\),
use the boundary-only candidate record, choose
\(qminus=qplus=0\), and put \(L=U=F(0)\).  If \(D=1\), \(F'\) is a
nonzero constant and the two boundary candidates suffice.  All selected
numbers in these cases have linear integer descriptors and rational
isolators.

Now suppose \(D\geq2\).  Compute the square-free part
\[
 g=\operatorname{sqfree}(A')
\]
by fraction-free gcd arithmetic.  The subresultant coefficients involved
are determinants of matrices of dimension \(O(D)\).  The determinant
expansion bounds their bit lengths by a polynomial in \(D+\tau+1\), so
\(g\) has degree at most \(D-1\), polynomial coefficient length, and is
computable in polynomial bit time.  By
\(\texttt{lem:integer-root-isolation-polynomial-time}\), one can compute
pairwise disjoint polynomial-length rational isolators for all real roots
of \(g\) in polynomial bit time.  Exact Sturm counts retain precisely
those in \((0,1)\), and the boundary records add \(0\) and \(1\).
Repeated roots of \(A'\) occur once because \(g\) is square free.

Apply
\(\texttt{lem:rational-polynomial-factorization-polynomial-time}\) to
\(g\).  For each retained interior root, attach the primitive irreducible
integer factor having the isolated root.  The factor together with its
rational isolator is an exact simple-extension representation of the
candidate and has polynomial bit length.

Introduce an indeterminate value \(z\) and form
\[
 E(z)
 =(Mz-A(0))(Mz-A(1))
   \operatorname{Res}_{q}\!\left(g(q),A(q)-Mz\right).
\]
The resultant factor is nonzero: over \(\mathbb Q(z)\), a common divisor
of \(g(q)\) and \(A(q)-Mz\) would have to divide the nonzero coefficient
\(-M\) of \(z\), and hence would be a unit.  Its Sylvester matrix has
dimension \(O(D)\), entries of \(z\)-degree at most one, and coefficient
bit length polynomial in \(D+\tau+1\).  Determinant expansion therefore
gives
\[
 \deg E\leq D+1
\]
and polynomial coefficient bit length.  Primitive and square-free
reduction preserve polynomial degree and coefficient size by the same
subresultant determinant bounds.

Isolate every distinct real root of the square-free part of \(E\), again
using
\(\texttt{lem:integer-root-isolation-polynomial-time}\).  For an interior
candidate \(c\), regard \(A(c)-Mz\) as a linear polynomial in \(z\) over
\(\mathbb Q(c)\).  The algorithm in
\(\texttt{lem:algebraic-extension-isolation-polynomial-time}\) isolates
its unique root \(F(c)\) in bit time polynomial in the displayed input
degrees and coefficient lengths.  Equality with a rational endpoint
\(\ell\) is decided exactly by reducing \(A(c)-M\ell\) modulo the attached
irreducible polynomial of \(c\); otherwise sign-guided refinement decides
the strict side.  Refine until exactly one value-root interval
\(J=(\ell,u)\) satisfies
\[
 \ell<F(c)<u.
\]
Such an interval exists because, after specializing the Sylvester matrix
at \(z=F(c)\), the shared root \(c\) supplies a nonzero kernel vector and
therefore \(E(F(c))=0\).  It is unique because the square-free value-root
intervals are disjoint and have count one.  Evaluate boundary candidates
by rational arithmetic and link them in the same list.

Candidates have equal values exactly when their exact links identify the
same root of the square-free value polynomial; otherwise their disjoint
isolators give a strict order after refinement.  Assign one label per
equal-value class and sort those labels.  This handles ties without
attempting to separate equal numerical intervals.  It also ensures that
an extraneous real resultant root with no feasible candidate link is
never selected.  The least and greatest linked labels determine
\(L,U,qminus,qplus\).  Sturm--Tarski sign records serialize each link,
tie, and strict comparison in the grammar of
\(\texttt{def:certificate-grammar}\).

Factor the square-free value polynomial and retain for each selected
endpoint the primitive irreducible factor containing its one-root
isolator.  An interior optimizer \(q_\circ\) is a root of \(A'\), so
\[
 [\mathbb Q(q_\circ):\mathbb Q]\leq D-1.
\]
Moreover \(F(q_\circ)=A(q_\circ)/M\) belongs to
\(\mathbb Q(q_\circ)\), whence
\[
 [\mathbb Q(F(q_\circ)):\mathbb Q]\leq D-1.
\]
Boundary optimizers and values are rational.  Thus each selected optimizer
and endpoint has algebraic degree at most
\(\max\{1,D-1\}\), with a primitive irreducible polynomial and rational
isolating interval as required.

Construct the two endpoint models by
\(\texttt{thm:endpoint-models}\).  If type \(t\) has \(R_t\) explicit
contexts and alphabet size \(k_t\), its number of positive atoms is at
most \(1+R_t(k_t-1)\).  Because the canonical explicit input lists all
these rows,
\[
 \sum_t R_t k_t=O(T).
\]
Consequently the number of entries in the context-by-atom mechanism
tables is at most
\[
 \sum_t R_t\bigl(1+R_t(k_t-1)\bigr)=O(T^2),
\]
and the source and target node references add \(O(T)\) entries.  Every
supported breakpoint is rational with description length bounded by the
input.  Per endpoint and type, the only possibly irrational adjacent
masses are \(q_\circ-a\) and \(b-q_\circ\), and they reference the single
polynomial-and-isolator descriptor already stored for \(q_\circ\).
Extension-field signs compare \(q_\circ\) with every rational threshold
and certify mass nonnegativity, including equality at a threshold.
Therefore \(Z\) has polynomial bit length and can be produced in
polynomial bit time.

Complete \(\Gamma\) with the canonical length-delimited digest, local
incidence records, exact gate identities, gcd and square-free identities,
Sturm counts, candidate-to-value links, tie labels, order records, and
exact source and target evaluations of the two finite models.  There are
at most \(D-1\) interior candidates, two boundary candidates, and at most
\(D+1\) distinct roots of the displayed value polynomial.  Even recording
all pairwise comparisons uses only \(O(D^2)\) records.  Every integer,
rational interval, polynomial, table, and arithmetic identity in these
records has bit length polynomial in \(N\), by the preceding determinant
bounds and the three cited polynomial-time algebraic algorithms.  Hence
\[
 |Z|+|\Gamma|\leq P(N)
\]
for one fixed polynomial \(P\).

It remains to prove acceptance rather than infer it circularly from
soundness.  On the constructed record, the digest matches by canonical
encoding; the copied incidence list is exhaustive; positive source
contexts and the rows in \(K\) agree by the instance hypothesis; the
recorded arithmetic replay ends at \(F\); the gcd, Sturm, resultant,
factor, isolator, link, tie, and ordering identities hold by their
construction; and the breakpoint models reproduce \(Psrc\) and evaluate
to \(L,U\) by \(\texttt{thm:endpoint-models}\).  Thus, on unfolding
\(\texttt{def:checker}\), every rejection guard is false and
\[
 Check(S,G,Rsrc,Psrc,\rho,a,B,Ictx,K,F,Z,\Gamma)=1.
\]
The checker traverses only polynomially many records.  Its rational
arithmetic, fraction-free gcd and resultant verification, Sturm
variations, factor and algebraic sign checks, table traversal, and
finite-model evaluations involve polynomially many integers of
polynomial bit length.  Standard bit arithmetic therefore bounds its
running time by another fixed polynomial in \(N\).  The sum of the two
bounding polynomials is one fixed polynomial bounding both quantities.
This proves certificate existence, the combined size bound, the
checking-time bound, and the algebraic-degree assertion.

We give the explicit forest instance.  In the source grounding, let
\(X_1,X_2,X_3\) be binary brake nodes with mutually independent fair
noises.  Let \(Y\) be a binary outcome whose supported conditional row
depends on the brake count \(k=X_1+X_2+X_3\) through
\[
 P(Y=1\mid X_1+X_2+X_3=k)=b_k,\qquad
 (b_0,b_1,b_2,b_3)
 =\left(\frac14,\frac5{12},\frac7{12},\frac5{12}\right).
\]
All displayed probabilities lie strictly between zero and one, so every
brake-count context has positive source probability and every source
joint cell on these four nodes is positive and rational.  The source law
is explicitly
\[
 P(X_1=x_1,X_2=x_2,X_3=x_3,Y=y)
 =2^{-3}b_{x_1+x_2+x_3}^{\,y}
       (1-b_{x_1+x_2+x_3})^{1-y}.
\]
It factorizes according to the acyclic graph and supplies the fair brake
row and all four outcome rows to \(K\).

In the target grounding attach two binary signal parents to each brake and
intervene to set all six signals to one.  The common brake type--context
row with two active signals is absent from every source occurrence; call
it \(rstar\) and write it as \((1-q,q)\).  The zero-signal brake row and
the four outcome rows are source supported, while the signal mechanisms
are removed by the intervention.  Hence \(rstar\) is the unique
target-relevant unsupported row.  The directed graph
\[
 \{\text{signals}\}\longrightarrow\{X_1,X_2,X_3\}
 \longrightarrow Y
\]
is acyclic, and its undirected ground graph is a tree with center \(Y\),
three brake neighbors, and two signal leaves adjacent to each brake.
The instance is therefore finite, Markovian, and type shared.

For \(B=\{Y=1\}\), the three target brake noises are independent and use
the same row.  Replaying the target factorization gives the Bernstein
polynomial
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 F(q)
 &=\sum_{k=0}^{3}b_k\binom3k q^k(1-q)^{3-k}\\
 &=\frac14+\frac12q-\frac13q^3.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Its derivative is
\[
 F'(q)=\frac12-q^2.
\]
The square-free cleared derivative \(1-2q^2\) has exactly one root in
\((0,1)\), namely
\[
 qplus=\frac{\sqrt2}{2},
 \qquad
 2qplus^2-1=0,
 \qquad
 \frac{70}{100}<qplus<\frac{71}{100}.
\]
The derivative is positive to the left of \(qplus\) and negative to its
right.  Direct evaluation gives
\[
 F(0)=\frac14,\qquad
 F(1)=\frac5{12},\qquad
 F(qplus)=\frac14+\frac{\sqrt2}{6}.
\]
Thus \(\texttt{thm:sharp-one-row}\) yields
\[
 \Theta
 =\left[\frac14,\frac14+\frac{\sqrt2}{6}\right],
 \qquad qminus=0.
\]
The upper value is the unique root in
\((48/100,49/100)\) of
\[
 144z^2-72z+1,
\]
whereas the conjugate root is
\(1/4-\sqrt2/6<1/4\).

For the lower endpoint, the brake-type breakpoint construction uses the
supported threshold \(1/2\) and the free threshold \(qminus=0\).  For the
upper endpoint, its distinct breakpoints are
\[
 0,\quad \frac12,\quad qplus,\quad1,
\]
with masses
\[
 \frac12,\qquad qplus-\frac12,\qquad1-qplus.
\]
The outcome-type breakpoints are all rational.  The inverse-threshold
mechanisms share these type tables across occurrences, and distinct ground
nodes receive independent copies.  The row calculations in
\(\texttt{thm:endpoint-models}\) show that both models reproduce the fair
source brake row, every supported outcome row, and hence every source
joint cell; their target values are the two displayed endpoints.  They
therefore serialize into a legal \(Z\).
\(\texttt{thm:certificate-completeness}\) supplies a \(\Gamma\) for this
fixed instance with
\[
 Check(S,G,Rsrc,Psrc,\rho,a,B,Ictx,K,F,Z,\Gamma)=1.
\]

Finally consider the two required rejection tests.  No feasible candidate
\(c\in\{0,1,qplus\}\) has
\(F(c)=1/4-\sqrt2/6\); indeed this conjugate lies below the already linked
boundary value \(F(0)=1/4\).  A record selecting it therefore fails either
the candidate-to-value link or the least/greatest linked-label check, so
soundness forces rejection.  If the positive critical point is omitted,
the certified Sturm count of \(1-2q^2\) on \((0,1)\) is one but the
purported exhaustive list contributes zero.  The candidate-exhaustiveness
check therefore rejects that record as well.

theorem.statement:
Under the present exhaustive assignment-level incidence grammar and
checker, the answer to the proof-carrying compiler question is negative.
There is a family indexed by \(k\geq1\) with explicit grounding size
\(O(k)\), treewidth \(w=0\), a directly event-relevant unsupported row
\(rstar\), and nontrivial equality event \(B\), for which the replayed
polynomial is \(F=1/2\) but every \(Ictx\) accepted by \(Check\) contains
\(2^k\) complete-assignment records.  Hence no compiler producing records
for this grammar can have time and output length polynomial in the
explicit grounding size and exponential only in \(w\).  This obstruction
does not rule out such a guarantee after replacing \(Ictx\) and \(Check\)
by a compact circuit-level incidence grammar and checker.
theorem.proof_tex:
The family and its count are supplied by
\(\texttt{thm:assignment-incidence-obstructs-width-compiler}\).  For its
\(k\)-th member, the pre-incidence input length is \(O(k)\), the target
ground graph is edgeless and has \(w=0\), and the equality query has
\(F=1/2\) while retaining direct relevance of \(rstar\).  Nevertheless
the definition of the present \(Ictx\) requires one record for each of the
\(2^k\) event-consistent complete assignments, and the present \(Check\)
rejects an omission.  Thus every accepted output has length
\(\Omega(2^k)\), and merely writing it takes \(\Omega(2^k)\) bit
operations.

If a compiler had a bound polynomial in the explicit grounding size and
exponential only in \(w\), then on this family \(w=0\) would reduce that
bound to a polynomial in \(k\), contradicting the preceding exponential
output lower bound.  The negative conclusion therefore follows for
\(\texttt{def:compiler-handle}\) with its current assignment-level
interface.  The cited obstruction makes no claim about a replacement
circuit-level incidence language, so the final qualification is
preserved.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix an integer \(k\geq 1\).  We construct the promised instance.  Take a fixed finite relational schema with two binary endogenous attribute types, called \(A\) and \(C\), and take the relational causal graph to have no directed edges.  Let the source list contain a grounding with one isolated node of type \(A\), whose rational source law assigns probability \(1/2\) to each binary outcome.  The corresponding parent context is the empty tuple, it has positive source probability, and hence its conditional row is recovered in \(K\).  Let the target grounding consist of isolated binary nodes \(X_1,\ldots,X_{k+1}\).  Nodes \(X_1,\ldots,X_k\) have type \(A\) in that supported context, whereas \(X_{k+1}\) has type \(C\) in a type--context key absent from every source grounding; designate that key by \(rstar\).  Choose the schema so that these are the only target-relevant type--context keys.  It follows that \(rstar\) is the unique unsupported target-relevant key.  Use the empty intervention and the compactly described event
\[
 B_k:=\{x\in\{0,1\}^{k+1}:x_1=x_{k+1}\}.
\]
All domains are finite, as required by \(\texttt{ass:finite-domains}\).  The target ground graph is edgeless, so it is acyclic by construction and satisfies \(\texttt{ass:acyclic-groundings}\).  The family of singleton bags \(\{X_j\}\), connected in any tree, is a tree decomposition: every vertex occurs in a bag, there is no edge to cover, and the bags containing any fixed vertex form a connected singleton subtree.  Its width is \(1-1=0\), so \(w=0\).

The schema, graph, and source description have constant size.  The ordered target node list has \(k+1\) entries and an empty edge list, and the equality event is specified by the indices \(1\) and \(k+1\).  Thus, in the fixed canonical encoding underlying \(\texttt{def:certificate-grammar}\), the combined input before materialization of \(Ictx\) has size \(O(k)\).

By the supported source row and \(\texttt{ass:type-sharing}\), every occurrence \(X_j\), \(1\leq j\leq k\), has conditional mass function
\[
 p_A(x_j)=\frac12,
 \qquad x_j\in\{0,1\}.
\]
For the unsupported binary key \(rstar\), write its shared row as
\[
 p_q(z)=(1-q)^{1-z}q^z,
 \qquad z\in\{0,1\},\quad q\in[0,1].
\]
Because the target graph has no edges and the intervention is empty, the truncated-factorization replay specified in the definition of \(F\) is
\[
 F_k(q)
 =\sum_{\substack{x\in\{0,1\}^{k+1}\\x_1=x_{k+1}}}
   \left(\prod_{j=1}^{k}\frac12\right)
   (1-q)^{1-x_{k+1}}q^{x_{k+1}}.
\]
When \(x_{k+1}=0\), the event forces \(x_1=0\), while \(x_2,\ldots,x_k\) may be chosen freely.  There are therefore \(2^{k-1}\) such terms, whose sum is
\[
 2^{k-1}2^{-k}(1-q)=\frac{1-q}{2}.
\]
When \(x_{k+1}=1\), the event forces \(x_1=1\), again leaving \(2^{k-1}\) choices, and these terms sum to
\[
 2^{k-1}2^{-k}q=\frac q2.
\]
Consequently
\[
 F_k(q)=\frac{1-q}{2}+\frac q2=\frac12
 \quad\text{for every }q\in[0,1].
\]
Hence the replayed dense polynomial is the nontrivial constant \(F=1/2\).  Here ``nontrivial'' means that the query is not a sure event: for example, an assignment with \(x_1=0\) and \(x_{k+1}=1\) does not belong to \(B_k\).  The constancy is instead the algebraic cancellation induced by the fair supported row at \(X_1\).

The key \(rstar\) is nevertheless directly relevant to the event-level replay.  Indeed, \(X_{k+1}\) is not intervened upon, the membership test defining \(B_k\) depends on its value, and every event-consistent complete-assignment term in the preceding sum contains exactly one factor \(p_q(x_{k+1})\) labeled by \(rstar\).  Thus the target-relevance field required by the definition of \(Ictx\) labels \(rstar\) as directly event-relevant even though summation cancels \(q\).

It remains to count the records forced by the grammar.  An assignment in \(B_k\) is obtained by choosing the common value \(x_1=x_{k+1}\) in two ways and then choosing \(x_2,\ldots,x_k\) independently in \(2^{k-1}\) ways.  Therefore
\[
 |B_k|=2\cdot 2^{k-1}=2^k.
\]
By the definition of \(Ictx\), its assignment-level portion contains a distinct record for every event-consistent complete target-assignment term.  By \(\texttt{def:checker}\), \(Check\) verifies exhaustive lexicographic indexing of precisely those records and rejects an omitted term.  Hence every \(Ictx\) accepted by \(Check\) on this instance contains at least \(2^k\) assignment records.  The fixed tagged, length-delimited representation in \(\texttt{def:certificate-grammar}\) assigns positive encoded length to every record.  Its output length is therefore \(\Omega(2^k)\).  In the standard sequential bit-cost model, producing that explicit output takes at least its length, and hence also takes \(\Omega(2^k)\) time.

Suppose, for contradiction, that a compiler for this grammar had time and output length bounded by a polynomial in the explicit grounding size and by an exponential factor depending only on \(w\).  Along the constructed family the explicit pre-incidence size is \(O(k)\) and \(w=0\), so the asserted bound would be polynomial in \(k\).  This contradicts the lower bound \(\Omega(2^k)\).  Thus no such width-sensitive guarantee is possible for the present exhaustive assignment-level \(Ictx\) and \(Check\).  The argument does not apply to a replacement circuit-level incidence grammar: as observed in \(\texttt{def:compiler-handle}\), variable elimination may represent the constant polynomial \(1/2\) compactly, while the lower bound proved here arises solely from the current requirement to materialize all event-consistent complete assignments.
